cards.name: Bit Planes
cards.summary: Reduces the image to its basic RGB colour components and turns gradual tonal changes into stark ones: each channel is cut down to a single bit plane, so the result is built from flat red / green / blue / cyan / magenta / yellow / black / white areas with hard banding where the original had smooth gradients. The Red, Green and Blue sliders pick which plane (0-7) of each channel is shown; which end of the slider gives broad posterized blocks and which gives fine, noisy banding was not verified in the harvest.
use_for: analysing gradients and banding in a bitmap
loud 8-colour retro / glitch-poster treatment of a photo
abstract colour-band backgrounds made from a soft photo or a gradient
avoid: you want a controlled number of tones: Effects/Transform/Posterize gives even, predictable bands instead
faces you need to keep recognisable: the colours become pure primaries and skin turns into blocks of red / yellow / magenta
scripting a vector object: Shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect needs a bitmap shape; run Object/Convert to Bitmap first or apply from the Effects menu
relying on the command string blindly: the harvest proved the command format on other effects but did not apply this effect's string in a test

params.name: Red
params.does: which bit plane (0-7) of the red channel is shown
params.typical: 0-7, default 0; which end gives broad blocks and which fine banding is unverified, so 4 is the safe first try

params.name: Green
params.does: which bit plane (0-7) of the green channel is shown
params.typical: same value as Red unless you want colour-shifted bands

params.name: Blue
params.does: which bit plane (0-7) of the blue channel is shown
params.typical: same value as Red unless you want colour-shifted bands

params.name: Apply to all planes
params.does: links the three channel sliders so one value drives all of them (from its caption; not verified)
params.typical: on (harvested default) for an even look; off to set channels separately

pairs_with: Effects/Blur/Gaussian Blur before it, to smooth noisy banding into broad shapes
Effects/Transform/Posterize as the tamer alternative
a Transparency on the effected copy over the original photo to tone the colours down

cards.name: Halftone
cards.summary: Gives the image the look of a colour halftone: the continuous-tone photo is broken into separate cyan, magenta, yellow and black dot screens whose dots grow with the ink amount, each screen at its own angle, so the picture reads as an enlarged print rosette. Max dot radius sets how big the largest dots get.
use_for: pop-art / comic-print treatment of a photo for a poster or social graphic
retro newspaper or screen-print texture on a background image
large-dot rosette pattern as a texture layer under type
avoid: real print screening for a press: this is a picture of dots baked into the bitmap's pixels, not an output screen; set screening in the print / PDF settings instead
small or low-resolution bitmaps: at the top Max dot radius (10) the dots swallow detail; enlarge or resample the bitmap first

a one-ink dot look: it screens four inks (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and Black angles); for single-colour dots convert a copy with Bitmaps/Mode/Black and White (1-bit) and pick a halftone conversion in its dialog
relying on the command string blindly: the harvest proved the command format on other effects but did not apply this effect's string in a test

cards.name: Psychedelic
cards.summary: Remaps the image's colours to bright, electric, unnatural hues (hot orange, hot pink, acid yellow, lime green) while keeping the shapes, for a trippy 60s / acid-poster look. Level sets how far the colours are pushed: the harvest audit measured a mean pixel change of about 47 at Level 39 and about 121 at Level 255, so higher is much stronger; the exact colours each tone lands on vary with Level.
use_for: acid / psychedelic gig and festival poster backgrounds
surreal colour treatment of a photo for an album cover or meme graphic
loud colour variants of one image for a pop-art grid
avoid: any natural or brand-accurate colour: the hue mapping is not controllable beyond Level; use Effects/Adjust/Hue/Saturation/Lightness or a duotone for designed colour
skin tones and faces you need to look human: they turn neon
values past the dialog maximum in a script: the audit showed Level 1030 renders the same as 255 (clamped), so stay in 1-255

params.name: Level
params.does: strength of the colour remap: the measured change from the original grows with Level (mean about 47 at 39, about 121 at 255), so even low values are clearly visible
params.typical: 127 default; 180-230 for an obvious acid look

pairs_with: Effects/Transform/Posterize after it, for flat screen-print style colour areas
Effects/Color Transform/Halftone after it, for a psychedelic comic print
a Transparency on the effected copy over the original to keep some natural colour

cards.name: Solarize
cards.summary: Folds the tonal range of each colour channel, a darkroom 'Sabattier'-style partial negative: every channel value v comes out as about Level x (1 - |2v/255 - 1|), measured on two renders (Level 40 and Level 200, within a few levels at every sampled point). Mid tones become the brightest part (mid grey 128 -> Level), both pure black and pure white go dark, and hues flip where a channel crosses the middle (orange 255,138,0 -> 0,184,0 at Level 200; the beige wall turns green). Level 200 gives a bright, psychedelic negative-colour picture, Level 40 a near-black one with faint glowing edges. By the same fit the default Level 127 keeps tones below mid grey and mirrors those above it, the classic solarize (inferred, not rendered).
use_for: surreal, Man Ray-style darkroom look on portraits or event photos
metallic / X-ray style backgrounds for music and tech posters
eye-catching negative-tone variants of a photo for a social carousel
avoid: a clean full negative: use Effects/Transform/Invert Colors
colour-critical work: solarizing reverses hues in the flipped tones
values past the dialog maximum in a script: the audit showed Level 1030 renders the same as 255 (clamped), so stay in 0-255
low Levels: Level 40 gave a near-black image (mean 22 of 255) on the render; start from the 127 default or higher

params.name: Level
params.does: the output brightness the mid tones fold to (Level 40 gave mid grey 40, Level 200 gave 200; black and white both go dark), a fold height rather than a flip point
params.typical: 127-255 (default 127); low values darken the whole image

pairs_with: Effects/Adjust/Brightness/Contrast/Intensity afterwards, to restore punch to the flattened mid-tones
Effects/Adjust/Desaturate first, for the classic silver solarized print

cards.name: Edge Detect
cards.summary: Finds the edges in the image and redraws them as lines on a flat single-colour background (white, black or another colour you pick), throwing away the fill tones: the photo becomes an outline sketch. Sensitivity sets how strongly edges are picked up; on soft, low-contrast images a higher value is needed for lines to show.
use_for: quick line-sketch version of a photo for an illustration base or colouring page
outline art on black for a neon / chalkboard style graphic (Black background)
a clean edge map to trace into vectors (Bitmaps/Quick Trace) for a logo or icon
avoid: blurry, low-contrast photos at low Sensitivity: few edges register and the frame goes almost blank
you want the photo kept under the outlines: Edge Detect replaces it (Find Edges and Trace Contour replace it too); apply it to a copy and lay that over the original with a Transparency merge mode
scripting a custom background colour: the harvested command template carries only ColorMode and Sensitivity, so the 'Other' colour (BackgroundColorItem) has to be set in the dialog
relying on the command string blindly: the harvest proved the command format on other effects but did not apply this effect's string in a test

params.does: background colour behind the detected edge lines
params.typical: White (default) for a pencil-sketch look; Black for glowing lines; Other with a picked colour

params.name: BackgroundColorItem
params.does: the custom background colour used when ColorMode is Other
params.typical: only with ColorMode Other; a brand colour or dark navy

params.name: Sensitivity
params.does: how strongly edges are detected and drawn
params.typical: 1 default; 6-10 on soft or low-contrast photos

cards.name: Local Equalization
cards.summary: Enhances contrast near edges by equalizing tones inside a small neighbourhood around each pixel, revealing detail in both light and dark regions; the result looks flattened and gritty, with exaggerated local texture and halos, like an overcooked HDR or a relief map. Width and Height set the neighbourhood size; smaller areas give a stronger, grainier effect.
use_for: pulling detail out of murky shadows and blown highlights in a dull photo (applied with a Transparency to tone it down)
gritty, grunge / HDR look for sports or action posters
texture maps and relief-like backgrounds from a photo
avoid: subtle tonal correction: at full strength it flattens the overall light and adds halos; use Effects/Adjust/Levels or Effects/Adjust/Tone Curve instead, or Effects/Adjust/Equalize for an even whole-image tonal spread
noisy or JPEG-compressed images: it amplifies noise and block artefacts
relying on the command string blindly: the harvest proved the command format on other effects but did not apply this effect's string in a test

params.name: Width
params.does: width of the pixel area around each pixel used for equalizing; smaller = more local, grittier
params.typical: 50 default; 20-40 for an obvious gritty look, 100+ for a gentler one

params.name: Height
params.does: height of that pixel area
params.typical: same as Width (tied when Square is on)

params.name: Square

params.typical: on (harvested default)
